title: Kuku sibzamini
subtitle: Persian potato patties with herbs and turmeric
excerpt: Kuku sibzamini are thick Persian potato patties made from grated potato bound with egg, flavoured with turmeric, fenugreek leaves, and spring onion. Fried until deeply golden on both sides, they are crisp outside and tender inside. They appear as a side dish, a main, and a Nowruz staple.
sourceNotes: Kuku is a family of Persian egg-based dishes, similar in texture to a Spanish tortilla but cooked as individual patties rather than a single round. Sibzamini means potato.

recipe.makeAheadNotes: The potato mixture can be prepared an hour ahead and left to sit. Fry close to serving.

content.text: Kuku sibzamini is the Persian answer to a potato cake. The mixture is simple: grated potato, egg, turmeric, and herbs. But the technique matters. The potato must be squeezed very dry before mixing, otherwise the patties will not hold together or colour properly.
The flavour comes from fenugreek leaves and spring onion rather than heavy seasoning, which keeps the patties bright and herbal rather than stodgy. They are best eaten hot from the pan.
Dried fenugreek leaves (methi) are sold in most South Asian supermarkets. They are worth keeping in the cupboard; they appear in many Persian recipes.

Place the grated potato in a clean tea towel and squeeze out as much water as possible. The potato should feel almost dry. Transfer to a bowl and add the beaten egg, spring onion, fenugreek, turmeric, salt, and pepper. Mix until fully combined.

Heat the oil in a wide frying pan over medium heat. Drop heaped spoonfuls of the potato mixture into the pan and press gently to form patties about 1.5 cm thick and 8 cm wide. Fry for 5 to 6 minutes per side until deeply golden and cooked through. Do not move them in the first 4 minutes or they will break. Cook in batches to avoid overcrowding the pan. Drain briefly on kitchen paper and serve immediately.

rows.cause: Potato not squeezed dry enough, or turned too soon
rows.fix: Squeeze the potato very thoroughly and wait until the underside is well set before flipping.

rows.symptom: Inside still raw when outside is golden
rows.fix: Reduce to medium-low after the first 2 minutes. The patties need time for the heat to reach the centre.

rows.cause: Oil too hot when patties added
rows.fix: Test with a small piece of mixture first. The oil should sizzle gently, not aggressively.

content.text: A small handful of fresh coriander or parsley stirred through the mixture adds brightness. For a more substantial kuku, add 100 g of crumbled feta to the mixture. Kuku sibzamini can also be served at room temperature as part of a mezze spread.
The uncooked mixture can sit covered for up to an hour before frying. The patties are at their best hot from the pan and do not hold well; reheat in a dry frying pan over medium heat if needed.

Kuku of various kinds appear on the Persian Nowruz table. Kuku sabzi, made with a large quantity of herbs, is the most celebrated version. Kuku sibzamini is the everyday one. It works as a side dish, a quick lunch, or a snack, and requires almost nothing to make.
